Who assesses and collects the tax

Alabama splits property tax duties between the state and its counties. Revenue's Property Tax Division writes standards and equalization procedures. Your parcel, though, gets valued at the county courthouse by the local assessing official, who handles every taxable real and personal parcel except utilities.

Billing and collection run through 67 county tax offices, so those offices are your first stop for anything tied to one parcel. For the state division, call 334-242-1525 or write to 375 South Ripley Street in Montgomery.

That split explains why twin houses in different counties can land on unlike bills. Each local taxing body sets its own millage, and the state doesn't flatten the gap.

Due dates and delinquency

Every year the clock starts October 1, which is both the lien date and the day the bill comes due. Pay after December 31 and you're late. From there the county works through a set sequence for any account that stays open.

WhenStage of an unpaid account
October 1Bill comes due
January 1Account is delinquent
FebruaryFile handed to the probate court
MarchProbate court sits
AprilProperty advertised
MayTax sale held

A statement that never arrived is no excuse. The Revenue Commissioner mails notices as a courtesy rather than a duty, and the debt exists either way.

How is the tax calculated?

The formula is simple: assessed value times millage. One mill equals a tenth of a cent, and each taxing agency applies its own mill count to the assessed value. Assessed value itself is a set percentage of appraised value, and that percentage varies with the property class.

Since millage changes by county and by taxing district, there's no statewide shortcut for guessing what a given house costs to carry. If you're trying to tell a buyer what to expect, get the parcel's assessed value and total millage from the county office instead of guessing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alabama house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How often are properties revalued?

All 67 counties run annual equalization. Each year the assessing official has to look at a quarter of the county's parcels, which means every parcel gets a fresh review once in a four-year rotation.

The aim is fairness between unlike properties and gentle yearly movement in value, so owners don't face a sudden spike when the cycle ends. Bills climb for two reasons. A millage increase needs a citizen vote or action by a taxing authority such as the County Commission. A higher appraised value can come from a court-ordered reappraisal or from economic gains in the county.

Either way, your bill may rise with no change to the house, and the buyer's first bill can differ from yours.

Reporting improvements

The reporting step is a trip to the Revenue Commissioner's office before December 31, where you or your agent sign a fresh assessment covering anything built or torn down by October 1. Reportable work includes:

  • New buildings or additions
  • Swimming pools
  • Extensive repairs, remodeling or renovations
  • A fireplace, extra bathroom, patio, deck, carport or garage you added

Routine upkeep doesn't count. Re-roofing, minor repairs and painting are the standard examples. Finished a project right before listing? Ask the county whether it's on record. A buyer's side may spot an unreported addition during review, and that can stall the deal.

How to appeal your valuation

A value that seems too high can be challenged by a written protest to the County Board of Equalization. You have 30 days, counted from the day written notice of the value reaches you. The rules sit in Code sections 40-3-20, 40-3-24 and 40-3-25.

  1. Begin by asking the county assessing official how the number was built.
  2. Get the protest on file before the 30 days end.
  3. Attach proof: contractor estimates for needed repairs, photos of damage, or sale prices of similar houses nearby.
  4. Ask the office if any payment is expected while your protest waits for a decision.

Disputes that outlast the board continue in court under section 40-3-25. After a denial, an Alabama attorney or the county office can lay out the options.

Selling soon? A protest already on file gives you a straight answer for buyers who ask about taxes, and a lower final value can mean a smaller first bill for the next owner.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alabama houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Which owners get relief?

Three kinds of owners skip the state share of the tax: people 65 or older, people who are permanently and totally disabled whatever their age, and blind owners. County levies can still apply. The claim goes to the local taxing official.

The exemption is tied to living in the home as a primary residence, so investors and distant heirs generally won't get it. Our Alabama homestead exemption guide walks through each type.

One more break: a manufactured home owner past 65 doesn't pay the registration fee on a home they live in, though the $5 issuance fee still applies.

Taxes and fees when you sell

Selling adds a charge that is separate from your yearly bill. Under section 40-22-1 the deed carries a privilege tax of 50 cents for every $500 of value, with any leftover fraction of $500 counted too. It's measured on the real purchase price, and it reaches only the part above a mortgage or vendor's lien that already paid mortgage tax.

  • A Department of Revenue form proves the actual price and travels with the deed.
  • The judge of probate does the math and collects before the deed is recorded.
  • Two thirds is sent to the state treasury, with one third staying in the county.
  • Knowingly holding back requested proof, or handing over false proof, brings a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater.

Who pays the current year's property tax is a contract term, so read that clause carefully. Near closing, ask the county if this year's bill is settled. A leftover balance is easy to clear at the settlement table, and much harder to deal with after you've handed over the keys.

What if you are behind on property tax?

Don't let it sit. The calendar speeds up after December 31, and once the file reaches probate court in February, a May sale is only a few steps off.

Back taxes tend to come bundled with other problems: deferred repairs, a title that came through an estate, or a tenant in the house. Then a sale may be simpler than a catch-up plan. Cash Home Buyers CA purchases houses in Alabama in their current condition, which means no repair list, and the overdue amount comes out of the closing funds. You can request an offer and think it over.

Before you start phoning around, collect the parcel number, the balance the county shows today, and any letter from the probate court. Those three items let anyone quote a payoff.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When are property taxes due in Alabama?

They come due October 1 and turn delinquent after December 31. October 1 is also the lien date.

Who do I contact about my Alabama property tax bill?

Call your county tax office. Outside of utilities, all property tax is assessed and collected through the 67 county offices.

How long do I have to appeal my valuation?

You get 30 days from receiving written notice of the value. File a written protest with the County Board of Equalization in that time.

Do I still owe tax if I never got a bill?

Yes. Notices go out as a courtesy from the Revenue Commissioner, so a missing statement doesn't cancel the debt.

Do I have to report improvements to my house?

Yes. Sign a new assessment at the Revenue Commissioner's office by December 31 for anything added or removed on or before October 1. Painting and re-roofing don't need one.

Alabama Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alabama Homestead Exemption sale
  • Turn the Alabama Homestead Exemption offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Alabama House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What counts as a homestead

The tax code treats your home as a homestead when it is a one-family house you occupy yourself, along with up to 160 acres of land. The house must be your primary residence on the first day of the tax year you are claiming.

Sellers should read that carefully. A vacant house after a move, a rental, or an heir's house when the heirs live elsewhere falls outside it. A house its owner lives in fits, and the owner could get a lower assessed value, with a bigger break for some older and disabled owners. The legal text sits in Title 40 of the Alabama Code, sections 9-19 through 9-21, and the Department of Revenue publishes a homestead page plus yearly memoranda on the income tests.

The homestead types, H-1 through H-4

Act 2013-295 groups Alabama homestead relief into types labeled H-1 through H-4. An owner's age, income and disability status point to the right one.

TypeWho qualifiesBenefit
H-1Under 65 and not disabledTakes $4,000 off assessed value for state tax and $2,000 off for county tax
H-2Age 65 or older with adjusted gross income below $12,000 on the latest state return, or retired for permanent and total disabilityNo state tax, plus $5,000 off assessed value for county tax, school district tax included
H-3 (age 65+)Age 65 or older with net taxable income of $12,000 or less on the combined federal returnNo ad valorem tax at all
H-3 (disabled)Permanently and totally disabledNo ad valorem tax at all, whatever the income
H-4Age 65 or older with income over $12,000 on the latest Alabama returnNo state tax, plus the usual $2,000 assessed-value exemption on county taxes

Keep in mind these numbers refer to assessed value, not what a house sells for. Residential property is assessed at only a fraction of market value, which means a small assessed-value cut wipes out a far larger piece of the sale price from taxation.

Why neighbors pay different amounts

Each piece of the bill, whether state, county or school district, gets its own relief, so a pair of neighbors who differ in age can pay very different amounts.

State tax first: anyone under 65 gets up to $4,000 of assessed value off, with no income test. Those 65 or older, the permanently and totally disabled, and blind owners face no cap on the state exemption and no income test, under the same 160-acre ceiling.

Counties vary more. A county, a municipality or another taxing authority can add an exemption of its own worth up to $4,000 in assessed value, and county school tax applies to some owner categories but not others. The result depends on where the house is and who owns it. To learn what a buyer would owe, phone the local assessing office rather than assuming the statewide minimum.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alabama house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Where to apply

Go to your county office, not the state. Apart from public utility property, every property tax is assessed and collected by one of the 67 county tax offices.

  • Show that you own the house and that it is your primary residence.
  • For an age-based type, bring proof of age, and the return named in that year's memorandum if there is an income limit.
  • For disability, a doctor fills out a physician's affidavit confirming permanent and total disability.
  • Ask which type the office has on file for you.

The Revenue Department's site lists county contacts. If you are unsure which office handles your parcel, the Property Tax Division answers at 334-242-1525.

The principal residence exemption

Title 40, section 9-21 adds a combined state, county and city principal residence exemption. Two groups qualify: people 65 or older whose income on the combined federal return is $12,000 or less, and the permanently and totally disabled of any age.

Both groups get no maximum assessed value, a 160-acre land limit, and no county school tax. The disabled category has no income limit. The relief closely matches what the H-3 type describes.

What happens to the exemption when you sell

Nothing here lets you guess about a mid-year sale, so ask the county. The firm rule is occupancy: you must live in the home as your primary residence on the first day of the tax year.

In practice the test splits things. Had you lived there that day, your exemption for the year rested on that, and a later buyer who moves in begins with the county office. An investor who will rent or flip the house cannot meet the test, so an investor should price the property assuming full tax.

  • Ask the county how your sale date changes this year's bill.
  • Read the title company's statement to see how tax is divided between buyer and seller.
  • Save your exemption approval letter for the title company.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alabama houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Inherited a house

Heirs who do not live in an inherited house fall outside the occupancy wording, so assume the decedent's exemption has ended. When the earlier owner was 65 or older and paid little or no tax, the next bill can come as a shock.

Payment is due October 1, delinquency starts after December 31, and the County Revenue Commissioner need not mail a notice. A slow estate can let a bill go unpaid and grow into a bigger problem, so look at the account early.

Some heirs sell as is to avoid repairs, carrying costs and open questions. A cash buyer can close when you are ready and deal with the cleanup, which ends the tax clock running against you. Take your time comparing options, and decline any offer at no cost.

Dates to track each year

A short timetable governs the tax cycle. An exemption shrinks the amount owed but leaves every date where it is.

  • October 1 is when payment is due.
  • January 1 begins delinquency.
  • February sends unpaid accounts to the probate court.
  • March is when that court meets.
  • April brings advertising of the property for sale.
  • May is the tax sale.

Add the day you list or sign a sales contract, since that date affects how the bill is split.

Manufactured homes

Manufactured homes follow one different rule: owners over 65 skip the registration fee on an owner-occupied manufactured home, but they still pay the $5 issuance fee.

It sits apart from the homestead types and matters if you sell a manufactured home on land you own. The home and the land can be billed differently, so ask the county which fees and exemptions go with each.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Who qualifies for the Alabama homestead exemption?

You do if you own a one-family house, live in it as your primary residence on day one of the tax year, and hold up to 160 acres. How much you get depends on age, income and disability, across types H-1 to H-4.

How much is the basic exemption for owners under 65?

An H-1 owner receives $4,000 off assessed value for state tax and $2,000 off for county tax. Counties and other taxing authorities can add up to $4,000 of their own.

Do I apply with the state or the county?

At the county office. The state writes the rules, while counties do the assessing and collecting.

When are Alabama property taxes due?

They come due October 1 and turn delinquent after December 31. Because the County Revenue Commissioner need not mail a bill, the tax is owed even if no statement shows up.

Can I keep my homestead exemption after I sell?

Check with the county about a mid-year sale. Your buyer applies on their own, and the occupancy test asks who lives in the house on the first day of the tax year.

title: Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Cash Home Buyers in Alabama
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax sale
  • Turn the Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Alabama House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Alabama has no estate or inheritance tax

Estates of people who die after December 31, 2004 do not have to file an Alabama estate tax return. Chapter 15 of Title 40 is still in the code under the title Estate and Inheritance Tax, so the statute is on the books even though the filing duty has lapsed.

The old tax was tied to the credit that federal estate tax law once allowed for state death taxes. Federal legislation passed in 2001 phased that credit out, and with it went any state filing for deaths after 2004.

For heirs of an Alabama house, that means no state death tax stands between them and a sale. County property tax, the deed recording step and any income tax the estate owes still apply.

Income tax filings for estates and trusts

Fiduciary income tax is separate from any death tax. An estate that earns income after the owner dies, for example rent on the house or interest on a bank account, may have to file a fiduciary return. The main rules:

  • Alabama Form 41 is the Fiduciary Income Tax Return, and the filing duty comes from Section 40-18-29(a) of the Alabama Code.
  • Every resident trust with net income over $1,500 for the year must file.
  • Every non-resident trust with any Alabama-derived net income after deductions must file.
  • A trust that claims a qualifying net operating loss must file in the year of the loss to carry that credit into later years.
  • Grantor trusts have their own filing rules under Sections 40-18-25(g) and 40-18-29.

Executors should read the Form 41 instructions against the estate's own facts.

Fiduciary return deadlines and extensions

The Alabama fiduciary return is due the same day as the matching federal return, and a Saturday, Sunday or state holiday pushes that date to the next business day.

Trusts and estates get an automatic extension that follows the federal one, and the federal extension form must be sent in with the Alabama return. Extra time to file is not extra time to pay, so tax owed is still due on the original date.

Two e-filing triggers apply:

  • An estate or trust with 20 or more beneficiaries at the end of the taxable year must e-file that year and every later year.
  • A preparer who files 25 or more acceptable original fiduciary returns with software in a calendar year must e-file all of that preparer's fiduciary returns from then on.

The executor answers to the Department of Revenue for any income the estate earns.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alabama house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The estate tax waiver and the affidavit

Form EST-1, the Estate Tax Waiver, is still among the Department of Revenue's popular fiduciary forms. For most estates, though, the Alabama Code offers a simpler route. Section 40-15-13 lets the personal representative sign and record an affidavit in the county of the decedent's last domicile, and in any county where the probate estate is pending. It states that the estate is not taxable, or that it is taxable and the right copy of a federal estate tax return has been or will be filed on time.

The affidavit must begin by stating it is filed under that section, and must contain:

  • The decedent's legal name and Social Security number.
  • The decedent's legal residence, including county, and the date of death.
  • Whether a federal estate tax return will be filed.
  • The name and address of the administrator or executor.

Once it is recorded, people who hold or manage estate assets may transfer them in reliance on it without getting a waiver, unless they know or should know it is wrong.

Can the state have a lien on an inherited house?

In principle, yes. Section 40-15-13(a) gives the State of Alabama a lien for any tax and interest that is or may become due under the estate tax chapter, on everything the decedent owned at death, in whatever form it now takes.

In practice, estates of people who died after 2004 have no filing requirement, so there is usually nothing for the lien to secure. It can still turn up in the paperwork of an older estate or in a title search on a house whose owner died long ago.

Before you list, run through this short check:

  • Find the date of death. After December 31, 2004 means no Alabama estate tax return is required.
  • Ask the probate court whether an affidavit under Section 40-15-13 is already on record.
  • Keep the recorded affidavit in the closing file.

Taxes an heir still faces on a sale

Three Alabama items remain even with no estate tax: the property tax bill, the recordation tax on the deed, and income tax questions for the estate. Each has its own office and timing.

Property tax follows a statewide calendar.

MonthWhat happens to unpaid tax
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

A house that sits through an estate administration can slip past January 1 if nobody pays the October bill. Heirs weighing a quick sale usually want that bill current before a closing date is set.

The deed that moves the house to a buyer is taxed when it is recorded. Section 40-22-1 sets the privilege or license tax at 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, or part of $500. Only the value above any mortgage that has already paid mortgage tax is taxed. Two thirds goes to the state treasury and one third to the county treasury.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alabama houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

At the probate judge's office

The judge of probate in the county where the house sits collects the recordation tax and the recording fee, then records the deed. Section 40-22-1 requires the tax to be paid before the instrument is received for record. Points that matter to a seller:

  • A deed or similar instrument must come with proof of the actual purchase price. If the property was not sold, proof of actual value is needed.
  • The Department of Revenue developed a form for attesting to the price or value, and a person who uses it in good faith does not need other documentation.
  • If no proof is given, the judge of probate bases the tax on the most recent assessment and may add a penalty.
  • The penalty for deliberately withholding requested proof, or giving false proof, is $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater.
  • Deeds executed for nominal consideration to perfect title are exempt, and the judge of probate stamps them "No Tax Collected."
  • A problem with the price proof does not undo the recording or the notice that recording gives.

Heirs who deed a house out of a trust or estate should ask the probate office which category their instrument falls into before they arrive with a check.

Selling an inherited house for cash

A cash buyer can purchase an inherited Alabama house as it stands, so the heirs do not have to make repairs or clear out the property first. Confirm who has authority to sign. The personal representative usually handles that when the house is in probate.

With no estate tax return required for deaths after 2004, the closing checklist is short. Typical items are the recorded affidavit or letters from the probate court, a current property tax receipt, payoff letters for any mortgage, and the recordation tax paid on the deed.

If you have inherited a house, our team can talk through timing with you.

Frequently asked questions

Does Alabama charge an inheritance tax on heirs?

No. Estates of people who die after December 31, 2004 are not required to file with Alabama, and the state describes no separate tax on heirs.

Do I need an Alabama estate tax waiver to sell an inherited house?

Usually not for deaths after 2004. Section 40-15-13 lets the personal representative record an affidavit that the estate is not taxable, and people holding estate assets may rely on it unless they know it is wrong. A title company can tell you what it wants to see.

Does an estate file an Alabama income tax return?

It may. Form 41 is required of resident trusts with net income over $1,500 and of non-resident trusts with any Alabama net income. An executor should check the form instructions against the estate's facts.

How much is Alabama's deed recordation tax?

Section 40-22-1 sets it at 50 cents per $500 of value conveyed or fraction of $500, reduced by value covered by mortgages that already paid mortgage tax. Proof of the purchase price must accompany the deed.

When do Alabama property taxes become delinquent?

Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent January 1. Unpaid taxes go to the probate court in February and can be advertised in April and sold in May.

Where an eviction case is filed

Either the district court or the circuit court can hear it, depending on their established jurisdictions, and the case belongs in the county where the rented property sits. Under Section 35-9A-461(b) of the Alabama Code, eviction actions get scheduling precedence over every other civil case.

The Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure and the Rules of Appellate Procedure apply, except where the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act changes them. Put simply, an Alabama eviction is an ordinary civil case on a faster track.

The county line matters to an owner of a rented house. A property in Madison County is heard in Madison County, and one in Mobile County is heard there, even if the landlord lives elsewhere.

Steps from notice to writ

The usual path runs from a written termination notice to a lawsuit, then a judgment, then a writ of possession. The statute sets no single calendar for the whole sequence, so the timing below covers only the steps it addresses.

StepTiming or rule
Termination notice, unpaid rentLease ends if rent and late fees go unpaid seven business days after receipt
Termination notice, other breachTermination date at least seven business days after receipt, unless cured
Lawsuit filedDistrict or circuit court in the property county, with scheduling precedence
Appeal windowSeven days after entry of the district court eviction judgment
Writ of possessionIssues on the landlord's application, after a seven day automatic stay

Notice periods count business days, so weekends and holidays stretch them. The relevant sections are 35-9A-421 for the notices and 35-9A-461 for the court steps.

Serving the tenant with the lawsuit

Service follows the civil rules, with a fallback built into the landlord and tenant statute. If a sheriff, constable or process server cannot reach the defendant in person, Section 35-9A-461(c) offers two alternatives.

  • Hand the papers to any person who is sui juris, meaning legally able to act, and lives on the premises.
  • If a reasonable effort finds no one living there, post a copy on the door.

Posting triggers a mailing step. On the day of posting, or by the close of the next business day, the notice of filing goes out by first class mail to the premises' mailing address, or to the defendant's last known address if the premises has none. Service by posting is complete on the mailing date, and the return filed in the case should record both the posting and the mailing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alabama house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Appealing an eviction judgment

The deadline is seven days after judgment is entered. Any party can take a district court eviction judgment to the circuit court inside that window, and the statute sets the deadline despite the general appeal rule in Section 12-12-70(a).

A timely post-judgment motion under the civil rules suspends the clock. The full appeal time then runs from the date the order on that motion is entered, or from the date the motion is denied by operation of law under Rule 59.1.

Once either side appeals, the clerk sets the case for trial as a preferred case, to be heard within 60 days of the appeal being filed.

Does an appeal stop the eviction?

Only if the tenant pays rent into court. Under Section 35-9A-461(d), an appeal to circuit court or an appellate court does not block a writ of restitution or possession unless the tenant pays the circuit court clerk all rent properly payable under the lease since the date the action was filed.

The tenant must then pay each new installment to the clerk as it falls due while the appeal is pending. If the parties disagree on the amount, the court decides what is properly payable.

  • A missed payment lets the court issue the writ on motion and place the landlord in full possession.
  • When the appeal ends, the court directs the clerk what to do with the money paid in.
  • If the landlord took possession and the judgment is later reversed, the circuit court may issue a writ restoring the tenant, but not against a third party.

After the judge rules for the landlord

A writ of possession issues once the landlord applies for it, subject to a seven day automatic stay. Section 35-9A-461(e) applies that seven day period regardless of Rule 62 of the Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure.

A tenant who is removed under the writ and re-enters without just cause can be held in contempt, and successive writs may issue as needed to carry out the judgment.

An owner planning a sale around a tenant's departure should treat the seven day stay and a possible appeal as the first two moving parts. Then ask the court clerk or an attorney how the writ is handled locally.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alabama houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other rules that shape an eviction

Four sections of the landlord and tenant act come up often, and each is short.

  • Holdover (35-9A-441(c)): a tenant who stays past the term or termination without consent can be sued for possession. A willful holdover not in good faith can also cost up to three months' periodic rent or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus reasonable attorney fees.
  • Month-to-month notice (35-9A-441(b)): either side may end the tenancy by written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in it.
  • Retaliation (35-9A-501): a landlord may not raise rent, cut services or sue for possession because the tenant complained to a code agency, complained about maintenance, or joined a tenants' group. Suing over unpaid rent or other material lease violations remains allowed.
  • Security deposits (35-9A-201): deposit money may cover accrued rent and damages, with an itemized written notice and any balance delivered 60 days after the tenancy ends and possession is delivered.

Section 35-9A-201 also caps most deposits at one month's periodic rent, with exceptions for pets, changes to the premises and increased liability risks.

Selling a rented house during an eviction

Owners do it, and the practical question is whether a buyer will take the house with the tenant, or the court case, still in place. Some buyers insist on a vacant home. We can look at an as-is house while the process is under way.

Know four facts before you agree to anything: whether a termination notice has been delivered, whether a suit is filed, whether a judgment has been entered, and whether any appeal money has been paid into circuit court. Those answers tell a buyer how much time and risk remain.

We buy houses as they stand, rentals with tenant trouble included. Tell our team where your case is, and we can talk timing without asking you to fix, clean or list anything first.

Frequently asked questions

Which court hears an eviction case in Alabama?

The district or circuit court, depending on jurisdiction, in the county where the property is. Section 35-9A-461(b) gives evictions scheduling precedence over other civil cases.

How many days does a tenant have to appeal an Alabama eviction?

Seven days from entry of the district court judgment. A timely post-judgment motion suspends that period until the court rules on it.

Does an appeal keep the tenant in the house?

Not by itself. The writ can still issue unless the tenant pays the circuit court clerk the rent due since filing and keeps paying as each installment comes due.

What is the automatic stay on a writ of possession?

Seven days. After a judgment for the landlord and an application for the writ, Section 35-9A-461(e) sets that stay in place of the general one in Rule 62.

How is a tenant served if the sheriff cannot find them?

Papers can go to a person living on the premises, or be posted on the door if nobody is found. First class mail follows the same day or by the close of the next business day.

title: Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property
content:
Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property

Cash Home Buyers in Alabama
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property sale
  • Turn the Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Alabama House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

How Alabama organizes probate

Decedents' estates are handled under Title 43 of the Code of Alabama. Chapter 2, Administration of Estates, is the main procedural map, and its twenty articles follow the order of a typical estate. These are the ones a house seller meets most:

ArticleWhat it covers
2Grant of letters testamentary or of administration
3Notice of appointment of executors or administrators
4Bonds of executors and administrators
13Collection, inventory and appraisement of personal property
15Claims and debts
17Renting and sale of real estate
18Settlements and distributions
19Insolvent estates
20Probate Procedure Act

If you want to sell an inherited house, article 17 and the Probate Procedure Act in article 20 matter most, since they deal with how real estate can be rented or sold.

Who can sell an inherited house

Authority usually rests with the personal representative the probate court appoints. That person is an executor when a will names one and an administrator when there is no will. A buyer's title company will want to see the appointment before it relies on anyone's signature.

Section 43-2-843 lists what a personal representative may properly do, unless the will or a court order says otherwise. Several items bear on a house sale: holding assets until distribution, performing the decedent's contracts to convey land, paying taxes and other costs of administration, insuring the assets, hiring appraisers and attorneys, and leasing property for a term not over one year.

When the decedent had an enforceable contract to convey land, the representative may deliver a deed for cash, or deliver a deed in escrow so that the proceeds go to the decedent's successors when paid. A buyer's title company will ask to see that paperwork.

Who inherits when there is no will?

Intestacy rules decide the heirs when no valid will exists. Section 43-8-42 sets the order for everything that does not go to a surviving spouse, or for the whole estate if there is no spouse.

  • First to the decedent's issue, equally if they are of the same degree of kinship, or by representation if not.
  • With no issue, to the decedent's parent or parents equally.
  • With no issue or parents, to the issue of the parents or either of them, by representation.
  • If none of those survive, to grandparents and their issue, half to the paternal side and half to the maternal side.

That order is why one inherited house so often has several owners. If children share equally, every child has a stake in the sale, and the personal representative needs a clear route to the buyer.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alabama house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why probate sales take time

A house cannot be sold until a person has authority to sign for the estate, and the probate court grants it. Letters, notice of appointment, bonds and the inventory of personal property each get their own article, and any can slow things when records are scattered or relatives disagree. The section also allows a representative to insure estate assets, borrow or advance money to protect the estate, and park idle cash in federally insured interest-bearing accounts.

Claims against the estate come next. Article 15 handles claims and debts, article 19 addresses insolvent estates, and article 18 governs settlements and distributions. A representative who sells the house before sorting out the debts may face questions from heirs or creditors later.

Property taxes keep running meanwhile. They are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, and paying taxes and assessments incident to administration is on the list of things a personal representative may do.

What the deed costs to record

Section 40-22-1 puts a privilege or license tax on recording: 50 cents per $500 of value, counting any leftover fraction of $500, for instruments conveying property worth over $500. Value covered by a mortgage or vendor's lien that already paid mortgage tax comes off the taxable amount.

  • Attach proof of the real sale price, or the real value if nothing was sold, using the Revenue Department's form.
  • At presentation, the judge of probate calculates the tax.
  • Without proof, the tax follows the latest assessment, and a penalty can be added.
  • Holding back proof on purpose after a request, or supplying false proof, costs $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is higher.

One exemption covers deeds executed for nominal consideration to perfect a title. Before you assume yours qualifies, ask the county probate office how an estate transfer is treated.

Probate and property records

Each county's judge of probate doubles as the deed recording office. So one courthouse shows up twice, in the estate matter and in the real estate closing, and the office that opened the estate file is the one that records the deed to your buyer. Ask early what that office needs, because a missing paper there can hold up the whole sale.

Get these together ahead of the closing agent's request, and check with the probate office on which ones your estate needs:

  • Certified letters proving who may sign.
  • The recorded deed or other record showing the decedent held title.
  • The newest property tax bill and payment history.
  • Names and contact details for the heirs, when there is no will.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alabama houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps from appointment to closing

The order of events is fairly predictable. The probate court first grants letters, and notice of appointment follows. The personal representative then collects and inventories estate property, and debts and claims are sorted out. Only then does it make sense to line up a buyer, using the powers in section 43-2-843 and the real estate rules in article 17.

At closing, taxes and any mortgage are paid, the deed goes to the judge of probate for recording with the recordation tax, and the proceeds move toward settlement and distribution under article 18. Keep each paper in one file so the title company is not chasing the estate for anything.

When an as-is sale suits an estate

An as-is sale fits when the estate has no spare time, money or energy to fix up and market the house. Probate already brings court steps, creditor questions and family choices, and a house needing a roof, a cleanout or a rehab piles on.

Cash buyers accept the house as it stands, skipping repairs, staging and showings. Authority still flows from the estate, so the personal representative works with the probate court and an Alabama attorney on timing, approvals and the deed. Heirs may weigh an offer against a regular listing and walk away owing nothing.

Frequently asked questions

Do you always need probate to sell an inherited house in Alabama?

A house titled in the decedent's name generally needs someone with court-granted authority to sign, called letters testamentary or of administration, and a title company will ask to see them. Ask the county probate office whether another route fits your estate.

Who inherits if there is no will?

Under section 43-8-42, the estate goes to the decedent's issue first, then the parents, then the issue of the parents, then grandparents and their issue, after any share for a surviving spouse.

Can a personal representative sell real estate?

Yes, within the powers the will and court orders allow. Section 43-2-843 lists the transactions a representative may properly make, and article 17 of Chapter 2 deals with renting and selling real estate.

Are property taxes still due while the estate is open?

Yes. Alabama taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, and paying taxes is among the acts a personal representative may do.

What does it cost to record the deed, and who records it?

The judge of probate in the property's county records it and collects the tax, which under section 40-22-1 is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction of $500 on conveyances above $500, plus the recording fee.

Alabama Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House

Cash Home Buyers in Alabama
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Alabama Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alabama Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House sale
  • Turn the Alabama Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Alabama House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Is there a separate capital gains tax in Alabama?

No. Alabama taxes the profit on a house as part of ordinary income. The individual rate statute, Ala. Code 40-18-5, sets a single three-step schedule with no special capital gains rate, so a recognized gain is simply folded into the income that schedule covers.

Federal treatment is a different question. Check it with the IRS or a tax professional before you sign a contract.

How the gain is figured

The gain is the amount realized minus the adjusted basis. Under Section 40-18-7, a loss is the reverse: basis above the amount realized. The amount realized is the money you receive plus the fair and reasonable market value of anything else you receive. Section 40-18-8(a) then treats the entire gain or loss on a sale or exchange as recognized unless an exception applies.

  • Cash received plus the fair market value of other property received make up the amount realized.
  • Specified taxes paid in connection with disposing of property reduce the amount realized, under Section 40-18-15(a)(3)(h).
  • On an installment sale, Section 40-18-7(d) lets the gain portion of each payment be taxed in the year that payment arrives.

Alabama income tax rates

Taxable income is taxed at 2%, 4% and 5%, depending on filing status and income. The brackets from Section 40-18-5 are below. They apply after deductions, so a gain is never taxed by itself.

Filing status2% on taxable income up to4% on income over that, up to5% on income over
Single, head of family, married filing separately$500$3,000$3,000
Married filing jointly$1,000$6,000$6,000

Every dollar of taxable income above $3,000 for a single filer, or above $6,000 for joint filers, lands in the 5% bracket. This describes the statute and does not predict your bill, because deductions, other income and exclusions all change the result. Run the numbers with a preparer.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alabama house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Deductions that can reduce the tax

Alabama lets individuals deduct federal income tax paid or accrued within the year. Section 40-18-15(c) allows it, and on a large gain it can take a real bite out of the Alabama bill.

Section 40-18-15 also lists other deductions that sometimes line up with a house sale or the months after it:

  • State and local real property taxes, only to the extent they are deductible federally.
  • Interest on debt, limited to what is allowable federally.
  • Casualty and theft losses on personal property, following the federal rules.
  • Medical and dental expenses above 4.0 percent of adjusted gross income, instead of the federal 7.5 percent threshold.
  • Moving expenses, but only where the new principal place of work is in Alabama.
  • Up to $35,000 spent removing architectural or transportation barriers for people with certain disabilities.

The optional standard deduction is the other path. Under Section 40-18-15(b)(4), a single filer with adjusted gross income under $25,500 gets $3,000, and joint filers under $25,500 get $8,500. Both amounts shrink as income rises, down to $2,500 and $5,000. A large gain usually pushes income far past those thresholds.

Deferring or avoiding the gain

In a few cases, yes. Section 40-18-8 lists exceptions to full recognition, and some involve real estate.

  • Like-kind exchanges: when an exchange meets 26 U.S.C. 1031, Alabama determines the recognized gain under that section, as Section 40-18-8(c) says.
  • Involuntary conversions: if the taxpayer elects treatment under 26 U.S.C. 1033, as after a condemnation or destruction, Alabama follows the election.
  • Transfers between spouses or former spouses: gain or loss follows 26 U.S.C. 1041.
  • Transfers to a trust: no gain or loss is recognized on the transfer.

Alabama writes no rules of its own here. It points to the federal Internal Revenue Code sections, so the federal conditions control, deadlines included. An ordinary market-price sale to a stranger is covered by the general rule, and the gain is recognized.

Selling an Alabama home from out of state

A nonresident who sells Alabama real estate faces limits on some deductions. Section 40-18-15(e) restricts several of them to items tied to Alabama property or an Alabama business. Section 40-18-15(c) also prorates the federal income tax deduction by the share of adjusted gross income that comes from Alabama sources.

If you inherited an Alabama house and live elsewhere, ask your preparer to check both states' rules before you file.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alabama houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The Alabama deed tax

Apart from income tax, Alabama charges a recordation privilege tax on deeds. Section 40-22-1 sets it at $.50 on instruments conveying property worth $500 or less, plus $.50 for each $500 or fraction of $500 above that. The taxable value can be reduced by mortgages or vendor's liens on which mortgage tax was already paid. An instrument cannot be received for record until the tax is paid.

  • Proof of price: the deed must carry proof of the actual purchase price, using the Department of Revenue form.
  • No tax: deeds executed for nominal consideration to perfect title.
  • Penalty: $100 or 25% of the tax due, whichever is greater, for failing to provide requested proof or giving false proof.
  • Split: two thirds goes to the state treasury and one third to the county.

Property taxes at closing

Property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. If you sell partway through the year, your title company can show how the current bill is divided, since the closing paperwork should say who pays what.

Property tax is a separate subject from capital gains, but both land on the same settlement statement, and unpaid taxes can delay a closing.

How a cash sale fits the tax picture

A cash sale leaves the tax on your gain unchanged. What it changes is the timeline and the costs: you know the price in advance, you skip agent commissions, and the deed tax and recording still go through the probate office.

If you own an Alabama house you want to sell as is, perhaps after an inheritance, send us the address for a written cash offer. Talk to a tax professional about the gain before you sign.

Before you meet with a preparer, collect the closing statement, your records of what you paid for the house and any improvements, and a list of taxes and costs tied to the sale. Those records drive the basis and the amount realized, which are the two numbers the Alabama calculation starts from.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does Alabama tax capital gains on a house sale?

Yes, as part of regular income. Under Ala. Code 40-18-8(a) the entire gain is recognized unless an exception applies, and it is taxed through the 2%, 4% and 5% brackets in Section 40-18-5.

What is Alabama's top income tax rate on a gain?

The top rate in Section 40-18-5 is 5%. It applies to taxable income over $3,000 for single filers and over $6,000 for joint filers.

Can I deduct federal income tax from my Alabama return?

Yes. Section 40-18-15(c) allows a deduction for federal income tax paid or accrued in the year, and nonresidents get a proration based on Alabama-source income.

What is the Alabama deed tax rate?

It is $.50 for each $500 or fraction of value conveyed, under Section 40-22-1, and it is collected when the deed is recorded.

Does a 1031 exchange work in Alabama?

Yes. Section 40-18-8(c) says that when an exchange meets the requirements of 26 U.S.C. 1031, Alabama determines the recognized gain under that section.

title: Alabama Tax Sales: Redemption and Selling Before the Sale
content:
Alabama Tax Sales: Redemption and Selling Before the Sale

Cash Home Buyers in Alabama
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alabama Tax Sales sale
  • Turn the Alabama Tax Sales offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Alabama House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

The yearly tax sale timetable

Alabama taxes come due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31. After that the file goes to the probate court in February, the court meets in March, the property is advertised in April, and the tax sale happens in May.

MonthStage of the delinquent account
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

That calendar describes the traditional property sale. Some counties now use a different remedy, covered below, so treat the months as a guide and call your county's collection office for the actual dates on your parcel.

Who can redeem, and for how long

Redemption rules are in Alabama Code section 40-10-120. When the state bought the land, it can be redeemed at any point before title leaves the state. When anyone else bought it, you have three years from the sale date.

A wide group may redeem:

  • The owner, the owner's heirs or personal representatives.
  • A mortgagee, or a purchaser of all or part of the land.
  • Anyone with a legal or equitable interest, a tenant in common included.
  • A judgment creditor or other creditor holding a lien.

A minor or legally incompetent person gets one year after the disability ends, even if the three years have run out. A mortgage or lien properly recorded at the time of the sale carries an added right: its holder can redeem within one year from the date written notice of the purchase is served.

You may redeem part of the land sold as long as the payment covers your whole interest. And if the same land was sold again in later tax sales, redeeming the first sale means redeeming the later ones at the same time.

Redeeming land the state bought

Apply to the county probate judge and deposit the price the land sold for, eight percent interest on it, every tax found due since the sale with eight percent interest, and officer costs and fees. Section 40-10-121 sets this out.

The state never paid the later years of tax, so the county assessor writes an assessed value for each year since the sale onto your application. If you disagree, file a written protest with the board of equalization. It schedules a hearing after at least 10 days of written notice and sends the value it fixes to the probate judge.

When any of the land lies inside a municipality, you also deposit the municipality's unpaid taxes plus the municipal tax that went unassessed while the state held the land, with the interest that would have built up. Owners often miss this item when they estimate a payoff.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alabama house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Redeeming land a private buyer bought

For sales to someone other than the state, section 40-10-122 applies. You deposit with the probate judge the sale price plus eight percent interest per annum from the sale date, and on the part of any excess bid that is 15 percent of assessed market value or less. Add any taxes the purchaser paid, with eight percent interest.

If taxes assessed to the purchaser are still unpaid, pay those to the tax collector before you redeem. You also pay officer costs and fees and a $0.50 fee to the probate judge, and the application and payment can be made online.

Houses add more. If a residential structure stood on the land at the time of sale, you must reimburse the purchaser's casualty insurance premiums, paid or owed, and the value of preservation improvements, each with eight percent interest. Preservation improvements are work done to keep the property in proper repair. Valuing them follows a short routine:

  1. Make a written demand for a statement of improvement value.
  2. The purchaser has 10 days to answer with a figure.
  3. You have 10 days to accept it or name a referee.
  4. Referees confer, and if they can't agree they choose an umpire. The majority award is final between the parties.

You can take possession before paying the improvement and insurance amounts, but you must reimburse them before January 1 of the following tax year or the right in the property is lost.

Do all counties still sell the property?

No. Act 2018-577 let tax collecting officials sell a tax lien in place of the property. Baldwin County's Revenue Commission moved to lien sales beginning in 2019 with tax year 2018 delinquent properties, and every lien for unpaid real property tax there goes to public auction. Bidders use the GovEase platform through the county's tax lien auction page.

For an owner the questions stay the same: how much is owed, who holds the claim, how much time is left, and what it costs to clear. A lien sale and a property sale do need different paperwork, though, so ask your county revenue office which remedy covers your parcel.

Baldwin is one example of the lien route. Other counties may still run the traditional sale, so don't assume the rules match from county to county.

Recording and redemption in Jefferson County

The Jefferson County probate court takes documents at two locations. The Birmingham division is in the Jefferson County Courthouse at 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd., and the Bessemer division is at 1801 3rd Avenue North in Bessemer. Recording hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

The recording office can't run a title search and can't prepare or revise a deed. For lien searches and legal paperwork, use a title company or attorney. Redemption deposits go to the probate judge, so a call to your own county's probate office is the best first step for exact amounts.

How a pending tax sale affects your sale

You can usually sell ahead of the tax sale or during redemption if the buyer, or the buyer's title company, pays what's owed from the proceeds. The delinquent tax, interest and any redemption deposit show up as lines on the settlement statement.

Gather these before you talk to a buyer:

  • The parcel number and each delinquent tax year.
  • Whether the county sold the property or a lien, and the date.
  • The purchaser: the state or a private buyer.
  • A payoff figure from the probate judge or tax collector.
  • Any mortgage or lien holders, who may hold their own redemption window.

Time works against you. Three years for a private purchase sounds generous, but eight percent interest runs the whole stretch, and improvements and insurance paid by the purchaser on a house raise the payoff further. An as-is cash sale can clear the redemption amount at closing with no repairs or showings in the way.

Frequently asked questions

When do Alabama property taxes become delinquent?

Taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31. The delinquent file then goes to probate court in February, with a tax sale in May.

How long do I have to redeem after a tax sale?

Three years from the sale date if a private buyer bought the property. If the state bought it, you can redeem any time before title leaves the state.

What interest rate applies to redemption?

Eight percent. Sections 40-10-121 and 40-10-122 both use it on the sale price and on the other amounts the redeeming party owes.

Who do I pay to redeem?

The judge of probate in the county where the land sits. Section 40-10-122 also allows the application and payment to be made online.

Can I sell to a cash buyer before the sale or during redemption?

Often yes, if the amount owed can be paid from the proceeds and title can be delivered. Get a payoff figure first, and ask an Alabama attorney if a mortgage holder or other lienholder is involved.
